optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Backend API Engineer, Equipment Maintenance Services

professionalSummary.text: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and parts-availability service for the technician app, including idempotency keys to prevent duplicate work orders from retried syncs.
professionalSummary.witness: Developed and maintained the work-order API (Go) and the parts-availability service that queries depot stock for the technician app, including the idempotency keys added so that retried syncs did not create duplicate work orders.

professionalSummary.text: Owned the integration test suite for both services, adding replay tests from anonymized sync logs and maintaining CI pipeline pass rates.
professionalSummary.witness: Owned the integration test suite for both services, adding replay tests built from anonymised sync logs and keeping the suite passing in the CI pipeline.

professionalSummary.text: Lined up releases with app and platform teams in release reviews, with deployments executed by platform team's release engineer.
professionalSummary.witness: Lined up each release with the app team and the platform team in the release review; deployments to production were run by the platform team's release engineer, not by me.

professionalSummary.text: Kept the API change log current, noting hourly depot stock refreshes, and maintained the on-call hand-over checklist.
professionalSummary.witness: Kept the API change log current, noting for each release that depot stock was refreshed only hourly, and maintained the on-call hand-over checklist.

professionalSummary.text: Two and a half years on the service-platform team, managing work-order and parts services, integration tests, release line-up, and change logs.
professionalSummary.witness: Two and a half years on the service-platform team: work-order and parts services, integration tests, release line-up and the change log.

experienceHighlights.text: Idempotency keys implemented to prevent duplicate work orders from retried syncs, reducing support-ticket volume related to sync issues.
experienceHighlights.witness: Reference call with former engineering manager: said the idempotency change 'basically made the duplicate problem go away' and guessed sync failures dropped 'from a few hundred a week to a handful'; he said he was going by support-ticket volume rather than the platform's sync-failure metric.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Replay tests for work-order API and one release's entry in the API change log with traceable CI run numbers.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the replay tests for the work-order API and one release's entry in the API change log; CI run numbers are included so they can be traced.

skills.text: Go programming, API development, integration testing, release coordination, change log management.
skills.witness: Two and a half years on the service-platform team: work-order and parts services, integration tests, release line-up and the change log.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's direct involvement in developing and maintaining the work-order API and parts-availability service, owning integration tests, lining up releases, and maintaining change logs. The materials do not establish a measurable reduction in work-order sync failures against the documented weekly baseline, as the reference call cites support-ticket volume rather than the platform's metric.

decisionBoundary.statement: Human review required due to unverified claims about sync failure reduction and missing evidence for requirement req_a43cb3667b39.
